To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extent to which performance evaluation schemes incorporate decision-facilitating performance indicators is associated with the use by strategic business unit (SBU) managers of such measures for both feedback control and feed-forward control purposes.
the use of performance measures for decision-facilitating purposes, as opposed to decision-influencing, impacts on the strategic performance of organizations.

the extent to which performance measurement information is actually used by managers for feedback and feed forward control is influenced by the extent to which the performance information is decision-facilitating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of performance measurement in the development of organizational capabilities.
the role of performance information and its evaluation for the development of organizational performance.
how the use of performance measurement and performance evaluation information can influence the development of strategic capabilities and organizational performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the availability of broad based performance information is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for improving organizational performance.

the availability of performance measures that are strategically relevant to the business unit manager and the extent to which the organization evaluates these measures in its performance evaluation scheme are important in the use of these measures for feedback and feed forward control and ultimately the development of organizational capabilities and performance.

performance evaluation schemes that are not congruent with the performance information used to facilitate decision-making are unlikely to result in the effective use of performance measurement information and hence the exploitation of strategic capabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
performance measurement and performance evaluation are both important for organizational performance but they need to be integrated.
the availability of broad based performance measurement information has the potential to impact the performance of an organization.
the use of decision-influencing measures is positively associated with the extent to which managers use decision-facilitating information for feedback and forward control.
The main takeaway from our work is that

to the extent that performance measurement and evaluation schemes are designed to reflect decision-facilitating indicators it will increase the likelihood managers use these measures to manage performance, and this will in turn have a positive impact on organizational performance.
performance evaluation mechanisms are an important factor influencing the use of performance measures and that the extent of this use has important implications for organizational performance.
to encourage the use of multiple financial and non financial performance indicators it is important to design performance evaluation schemes that also reflect such indicators.
